text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — p99 latency breach for enterprise customer Valora (VPC, eu-west-1). SLO p99 500ms breached to ~3.2s, customer-facing errors increased. Paging on-call. Severity: P1

incident-bot: Paging on-call: sasha (rotation: infra-night).

sasha: saw the alert. joining. any immediate blast radius?

mike_r: Valora is ondedicated pool 'valora-dedicated-3' in eu-west-1. We're seeing sustained queue depth and many in-flight KV cache misses. p95 up to 1.1s, p99 3.2s.

anita: customer cs already reported timeouts for 2 of their production routes. They're seeing 500s during checkout flows. Karen, any direct customer comms?

karen_cs: Yes, Valora on call is in the thread. I've told them we're investigating and will follow up in <30m. They want ETA for mitigation.

lia_devops: grabbing pool metrics. looks like GPU utilization at 98% on two hosts, other hosts idle because of tenant affinity. There's a hot-tenant pattern — Valora's tenant queue exploded (burst from marketing push).

sean_sre: can we evict lower-priority tenants or enable tenant isolation throttle? we have per-tenant rate control but not yet applied to this pool.

sasha: immediate mitigations: 1) enable tenant-level rate-limit for Valora (drop to 60% of normal) 2) route a percentage of Valora traffic to warm spare pool in eu-west-2 3) enable automatic model-fallback to smaller quantized variant for non-critical endpoints.

mike_r: I can push temp rate-limit. please confirm exact key. is it tenant_id=valora-prod?

anita: yes tenant_id=valora-prod. Also note some routes are latency-sensitive (checkout) vs background (analytics). we should only route non-checkout to fallbacks.

sasha: agreed. Mike, do the rate-limit and add a route rule for path /api/v1/checkout to keep on primary pool. Other endpoints get fallback.

mike_r: doing now. command: \n```\nredwoodctl tenant-rate-limit set --tenant valora-prod --rate 60% --scope pool:valora-dedicated-3\n```\nApplied. \n\nmike_r: route rule applied: send 30% of non-checkout traffic to warm spare pool (eu-west-2) using traffic-split policy.

lia_devops: warm spare pool warmed, KV cache pre-warmed for common prefixes. starting cross-region routing. watch for increased egress.

incident-bot: NOTE: routing rule created (id: rsplit-2381-valora).

sean_sre: watching metrics — p99 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.8s within 90s of rate-limit. good sign. p95 now ~760ms.

karen_cs: Valora wants an explanation and ETA. I can tell them we've mitigated to reduce customer impact and are doing additional capacity work; ETA for stable baseline ~45-60m. OK?

anita: yep that's accurate. We'll keep real-time updates. Sasha, can you own postmortem?

sasha: will own postmortem. logging everything here. initial hypothesis: customer-triggered traffic spike + tenant affinity constraints caused local resource saturation and KV cache churn leading to high tail latencies.

mike_r: noticed a pattern in access logs: many long-tail prompts with large context lengths from valora-prod-collector. that's increasing token compute per request. snippet from logs:\n```\n2026-03-15T02:12:39Z valora-prod-collector request_id=abcd1234 ctx_len=8192 model=mistral-large\n2026-03-15T02:12:40Z valora-prod-collector request_id=abcd1235 ctx_len=8200 model=mistral-large\n```\nWe should throttle or transform those clients.

anita: can we apply prompt-length limiter for non-checkout routes as a short term?

sasha: yes. Add transformer that rejects or truncates >4k tokens with 429 for analytics endpoints. Mike?

mike_r: patching policy now: \n```\nredwoodctl tenant-policy set --tenant valora-prod --policy 'truncate_context:4096' --routes '^/api/v1/(analytics|ingest)'\n```\nPolicy in place.

lia_devops: after throttles + routing + fallback, CPU/GPU pressure reduced. one host still showing kernel preemption spikes — investigating OS-level interrupts.

sean_sre: if kernel jitter persists, we may drain that host and re-schedule. start drain candidate: gpu-host-euw-12.

mike_r: initiated drain. 

incident-bot: Host drain started (gpu-host-euw-12). unevictable pods: 2 (long-running stateful). will finish in ~5m.

karen_cs: Valora asking for rollback if this impacts features (they're okay with 429s on analytics). They want a follow-up call in 30m. I'm scheduling.

sasha: status check: p99 now ~640ms, p95 320ms. Errors down by 87%. Good. Keep monitoring for 30m then start gradual rollback of emergency limits if stable.

anita: note for postmortem: dedicated pool affinity allowed excessive concentration. recommend: a) enable pre-configured tenant soft-limits for enterprise pools b) automatic burst-absorbing warm-sparing cross-region policy c) improve prompt-length enforcement by default for ingestion routes.

mike_r: saving config changes to git: branch fix/valora-p99-containment.

lia_devops: kernel issue on drained host shows bad NVMe wear causing I/O stalls — replacing host with spare. ops ticket created: OPS-9921.

sean_sre: handoff: I'm taking 2-hour follow-up window to validate stability and own the incident until postmortem. Sasha you'll own the write-up.

sasha: ACK. I'll draft RCA and mitigation plan.

karen_cs: Closing loop with Valora: told them we've reduced customer-facing impact, have a temporary mitigation, working on permanent fixes. They requested root cause + timeline within 24 hours.

incident-bot: Incident updated: mitigated -> monitoring. severity downgraded to P2.

sasha: final notes: timeline, commands executed, metrics before/after, config diffs will go to the postmortem doc. We'll include recommended follow-ups and owners.

mike_r: any outstanding actions?

sean_sre: I'll verify warm-spare routing performance and confirm no cross-region SLO regressions. lia will track hardware replacement. anita will scope policy defaults. karen will manage customer comms.

karen_cs: Valora wants a 1:1 review tomorrow. I'll book for 14:00 UTC.

sasha: thanks all. moving to post-incident channel after 30m stable.

oncall-bot: This thread will auto-close in 72h unless updated.
